decision.explanation: The series is geometric with first term 1/2 and common ratio 4. Thus S_N=(1/2)(4^N-1)/(4-1)=(1/6)(4^N-1), which is option c.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a series $\frac{1}{2}+2+8+⋯?$
after.worked_solution:
Note that $\frac{1}{2}+2+8+⋯$ is the sum of a geometric series since the ratio of any two consecutive terms is constant.

First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{2}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case ${a}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}$ and $r=4.$ Substituting these values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}(1-{4}^{N})}{1-4} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}(1-{4}^{N})}{-3} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{3}\cdot ({4}^{N}-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}({4}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

What is the sum of the first N terms of a series 12+2+8+⋯?

a
16(1−4N)
b
(46)N−16
c
16(4N−1)
d
(46)N+16
e
16(4N+1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Note that 12+2+8+⋯ is the sum of a geometric series since the ratio of any two consecutive terms is constant.

First, we determine the common ratio r for this geometric series:

r=a2a1=2(12)=4

The sum of the first N terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

SN=a1(1−rN)1−r.

In this case a1=12 and r=4. Substituting these values into the formula for SN gives the following:

SN=a1(1−rN)1−r=12(1−4N)1−4=12(1−4N)−3=(12)3⋅(4N−1)=16(4N−1)

content.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a series $\frac{1}{2}+2+8+⋯?$
content.worked_solution:
Note that $\frac{1}{2}+2+8+⋯$ is the sum of a geometric series since the ratio of any two consecutive terms is constant.

First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{2}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case ${a}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}$ and $r=4.$ Substituting these values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}(1-{4}^{N})}{1-4} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}(1-{4}^{N})}{-3} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{3}\cdot ({4}^{N}-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}({4}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{15}{3} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case ${a}_{1}=3$ and $r=5.$ Substituting these values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives the following:

$$

content.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series $3+15+75+⋯\,?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{15}{3} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case ${a}_{1}=3$ and $r=5.$ Substituting these values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{3(1-{5}^{N})}{1-5} \\  & =\frac{3(1-{5}^{N})}{(-4)} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}(1-{5}^{N}) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}({5}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

What is the sum of the first N terms of a geometric series if the 4th term is 192 and the common ratio is 4?

a
3N−1
b
4N−12
c
4(3N−1)
d
4N−1
e
3(4N−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We use the formula for the nth term of a geometric sequence to determine a1:

an=a1rn−1192=a1⋅4(4−1)192=64a1a1=3

The sum of the first N terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

SN=a1(1−rN)1−r.

In this case, a1=3 and r=4. Substituting our values into the formula for SN gives:

SN=3(1−4N)1−4=3(−3)(1−4N)=−(1−4N)=4N−1

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Formula for the Sum of a Geometric Series Given an Arbitrary Term and the Common Ratio
content.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $4$th term is $192$ and the common ratio is $4?$
content.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine ${a}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 192 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {4}^{(4-1)} \\ 192 & =64{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=3$ and $r=4.$ Substituting our values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{3(1-{4}^{N})}{1-4} \\  & =\frac{3}{(-3)}(1-{4}^{N}) \\  & =-(1-{4}^{N}) \\  & ={4}^{N}-1\end{aligned}
$$
